steps.text: Gather all ingredients. Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease and flour two 9-inch round baking pans.
Stir sugar, flour, cocoa, baking powder, baking soda, and salt together in a large bowl.
Add eggs, milk, oil and vanilla; mix for 2 minutes on medium speed with an electric mixer.
Stir in the boiling water. The batter will be thin.
Pour evenly into the prepared pans.
Bake in the preheated oven until a toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean, about 30 to 35 minutes. Cool in the pans for 10 minutes, then transfer to a wire rack to cool completely.

raw_recipe.headline: One Bowl Chocolate Cake
raw_recipe.description: This homemade chocolate cake recipe is easy to make in one bowl; top with your favorite chocolate frosting for a fudgy, moist chocolate layer cake.

review.reviewBody: I couldn't ask for any better! I used a 9x13 pan and baked it for 40 minutes. I just made this for the 2nd time and this time I upped the cocoa to 1 cup... I'm REALLY glad I did! The cake is great with the amount called for, but after trying more to see the difference, I definitely think 1 cup is the magic amount. If I could give it more than 5 stars, I would. I used the "Buttercream Icing" recipe (pictured) from Sharon on this website. Incredible together!

Great recipe easy to follow and the kids loved it!!! Only changes made was 1/2 cup of boiling water instead of 1 full cup, also 1 cup of Sugar instead of 2 full cups and baked for 40mins in a large round pan. My family prefers less sweet. But came out full of chocolate flavour, moist and new family fave!!! Thank you so much!!

I substituted the oil for 90grams of melted butter, and added 1 1/2 teaspoons of instant coffee. I mixed all of the wet ingredients separately so I could whisk the milk and eggs together and of course, the butter hit the milk and solidified, so I warmed up the wet ingredients by 'bain marie' and then added it to the dry. I mixed them both together before adding the boiling water. I only had one cake tin so ended up baking all in one for almost an hour. I started at 180ºC then knocked it down to about 170ºC after 20 minutes. I used chocolate butter icing for the middle, top and sides, and topped with various chocolate pieces. It was hugely successful, moist and delicious! Everyone loved it including the kids who rated it super high! Amazing recipe; don't panic about the water - it really does work!!
Perfect

Make this with high quality ingredients, measure your ingredients properly, err on the underbake/undermix side, and use an oven thermometer to ensure you're baking at the right temp. It's easy, moist, tender, and full of chocolate flavor! Also amazing with about a teaspoon of instant coffee powder. I've even made this with King Arthur's gluten-free measure-for-measure flour and it's still SO MOIST AND FLAVORFUL!

Okay, I made this today.It is better than any fancy restaurant cake.I followed the directions exactly.Except I put in a full cup of cocoa and I added a teaspoon of instant coffee to the hot water, This\nCake came out so chocolatey.It came out moist.It came out like a black forest cake that you would get in a restaurant.I am so astounded and happy and pleased.It is the best thing I've ever made in my life.And my gosh , the taste is outrageously good.

I substituted boiling water for Black coffee. Also let sit in the cake pans overnight and then removed from the pans. I use 6" pans and get 2 cakes (3 layers with this recipe). I also use a combo of black cocoa (1/3)and normal (2/3)cocoa. Not too sweet but the moistest and tastiest cake you will ever bake. This is a keeper recipe!!

I also use a combo of black cocoa (1/3)and normal (2/3)cocoa. Not too sweet but the moistest and tastiest cake you will ever bake. This is a keeper recipe!!
My go to cake...but I use buttermilk and 1 cup of cocoa. I put it all in one cake silicon pan for 50 minutes and it comes out beautifully every time. Kids love it!!!

This worked well for us, during a sweets craving. l used a whisk to whip everything together; sifted dry ingredients then whisked the wet together before combining the two gently, there were still lumps. Additionally, I added 1/2 tsp instant expresso to the boiling water [only used 2/3 cup boiling water] also cut the sugar using 1 cup only and used BUTTERmilk. Also I substituted ghee instead of veggie oil. It is DELICIOUS; grandkids help sprinkle homemade confection sugar between layers and lightly on top!

Worked out great. Did it slightly different. I added a teaspoon of coffee to the boiling water then added the boiling water to the wet mix whisking as I went. Then I sieved the wet mix into the dry mix in a stand mixer and just mixed the whole thing for 2 minutes. Put it in my cake pans and it turned out perfect. Definitely a keeper.

I made this along time ago. And every time I make a chocolate cake I use this recipe with modifications. I dont use boiling water, it makes it stick to the pan even if you butter and flour. I also use more coaco powder, I use olive oil, and not refined white sugar. With my modifications it's a keeper and make it often. Store bought has nothing on this cake... its rich in flavor and moist and holds shape well for my chocolate frosting.
I was worried about the boiling water, but this cake came out moist and fluffy. I added nuts they worked. I also added cherry pie fillin to the icing. Tasted yummy.

I made in two loaf pans this time and it had to bake for 50 minutes. I coupled it with an easy peanut butter frosting!! Wow! No matter what pan I bake this in it’s a great recipe. I’ve done cupcakes with it they came out moist and bouncy.

I substituted a boiling cup of strong brewed coffee for the cup of boiling water. The batter does look very thin but comes out perfectly. Husband raved over this and the homemade mocha buttercream (2 sticks butter, 4 cups powdered sugar, cocoa powder, 2tbsp brewed coffee, vanilla, salt) I made with it.

This cake was easy to make and delicious! Only bad thing was it took a while to bake, after 40 minutes the outside was cooked and the inside was completely wet, but I put tin foil on top and it only took another 20 minutes to get to perfection!

Delicious cake and very easy to make. I used a 9 x 13 pan and baked it for 50 minutes. I didn't ice it - instead I served it with berry compote (strawberries and blueberries) and whipped cream. Very nice.

Cake was sooo good. Will now be my go-to recipe for chocolate cake. Great results with little effort. I’d rather follow a recipe that requires less than gfollow a recipe that requires more and get great results as well. If it didn’t come out right for you then it was something you didn’t do correctly. Thumbs up!

I love this recipe! I did alter it slightly by changing all purpose flour out to cake flour since I was oddly out of all purpose when I made it but it was so flavorful even a friend who doesn't like cake enjoyed it!
Good texture and sweet although I put 1 cup sugar
